First, AG’s global revenue has reached its highest mark, and that growth has continued across all of its offices despite geopolitical uncertainty and heightened regulations. That combination matters to me: it shows a firm that can expand while managing real-world pressure, which I read as evidence of rigorous training and support for ambitious people who want to take on high-profile work and still progress.

Second, I am particularly interested in disputes. AG’s disputes resolution practice has been recognised as Disputes Resolution Team of the Year, and the chance to work in that environment is a major attraction. Through Model United Nations I practised international policy negotiation, building listening and negotiation skills while advocating for a position. That experience sharpened my appetite for high-quality disputes training and for advocacy in demanding forums. The prospect of representing clients before the Supreme Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union at AG therefore appeals strongly.

Third, AG’s training contract appears distinctive in the responsibility given to trainees, including management roles for legal streams and client meetings. That early ownership is exactly the kind of stretch I want in order to build the skillset of a successful commercial lawyer.

Together, peak growth under pressure, a leading disputes offering linked to my MUN experience, and meaningful trainee responsibility make AG my chosen firm.
